subject.title: [Bug]: Performance degradation in session memory sync: full delete-reinsert pattern for growing JSONL files

question: Should session-memory optimization use current-schema incremental append indexing, or should maintainers prefer batching, compaction, or retention limits instead?
rationale: The source-level bug is real, but the permanent fix affects memory schema/state, chunk overlap semantics, session compaction behavior, and existing source-wide batching, so automation should not choose the architecture alone.

options.title: Sponsor current-schema incremental sync
options.body: Design an incremental path against memory_index_sources and memory_index_chunks, with tests for append, overlap, compaction/reset, FTS/vector, and source-wide batching.

options.title: Limit through batching or retention
options.body: Keep full-file rebuild semantics but reduce user impact through existing batching plus explicit compaction or retention policy work.

options.title: Close as not planned
options.body: Accept full transcript rebuilds as the current memory-model tradeoff and close both the issue and stale PR attempts with that rationale.

recommendation.title: Sponsor current-schema incremental sync
recommendation.body: Design an incremental path against memory_index_sources and memory_index_chunks, with tests for append, overlap, compaction/reset, FTS/vector, and source-wide batching.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history puts vincentkoc closest to the memory schema and storage migration choices that constrain the durable fix.
